title: A protocol for qualitative and quantitative measurement of endosomal processing using hot spot analysis
protocol: Wash splenic murine DC three times in 20 mL PBS and pellet for 10 min at 500 × g.
Resuspend the cellular pellet in 1 mL PBS containing 0.25 M sucrose, 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4) supplemented with complete protease inhibitor cocktail (containing 1 mM EDTA).
Homogenize cells in a Dounce homogenizer twice for 10 minutes each on ice.
Spin the homogenate at 150 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C using a desktop microcentrifuge.
Examine the pellet under a microscope to ensure complete cellular lysis.
Combine supernatants from two rounds of homogenization steps (2 mL).
Load combined supernatants above 9 mL of 27% Percoll laid over 1 mL of 2.5 M sucrose in 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4) cushion.
Centrifuge for 1 hour at 34,000 × g at 4°C using a Beckman Optima XPN 100K Ultracentrifuge and SW Ti41 rotor.
Remove the band above the sucrose cushion with a P1000 pipette to obtain the total lysosomal fraction.
Lay 9 mL of 10% Percoll on top of 1 mL of 2.5 M sucrose in 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4) cushion for further separation.
Centrifuge the interface at 34,000 × g for 1 hour at 4°C using a Beckman Optima XPN 100K Ultracentrifuge and SW Ti41 rotor.
Collect the late endosomal fraction at the interface between the Percoll and sucrose layer.
Wash the late endosomal fraction three times with 30 mL of PBS containing 0.25 M sucrose and 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4) for 10 min each time at 3000 × g and 4°C.
Determine the total protein concentration in a small aliquot from the late endosomal fraction using the BCA assay.
Incubate native OVA and HEL with purified late endosomes from control C57BL/6J or Ob/Ob mice in sodium acetate buffer for 6 and 12 h at 37°C.
Quench the proteolysis reaction with 0.5% acetonitrile and 5% formic acid.
Extract processed peptides through a 10 kDa MWCO using centrifugal filter units by centrifugation at 8000 g for 10 min.
Purify the extracted peptides using C18 zip tips.
Lyophilize purified peptides using a Speed-Vac microcentrifuge.
Reconstitute peptide extracts in 25 μL of 5% acetonitrile containing 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid.
Load 3.0 μL of reconstituted sample onto a nano-ACQUITY UPLC precolumn at 4.0 μL/min for 4.0 min using a 100 μm I.D. fused-silica column packed with 5 μm (200 Å) Magic C18AQ material.
Develop a linear gradient from 5% solvent A to 35% solvent B in 90 minutes, where solvent A is water containing 0.1% formic acid and solvent B is acetonitrile containing 0.1% formic acid.
Introduce ions by positive electrospray ionization via liquid junction into a Q Exactive hybrid mass spectrometer.
Acquire mass spectra over m/z 300–1750 at a resolution of 70,000 (m/z-200).
Select the top 10 most abundant precursor ions in each scan for tandem mass spectrometry by HCD fragmentation using an isolation width of 1.6 Da and collision energy of 27.
Perform data-dependent acquisition with a resolution of 17,500 for tandem mass spectrometry.
Filter DDA raw files using Peaks 8.5/X/X+ software.
De novo sequence filtered raw files.
Assign protein IDs by searching against the Swiss-Prot FASTA database.
Apply "no enzyme" setting for peptide search.
Set parent mass tolerance to 15 ppm or lower (10–12 ppm) with monoisotopic mass.
Configure fragment ion mass tolerance of 0.05–0.1 Da depending on the mass spectrometer used.
Set variable modifications including methionine, lysine, proline, arginine, cysteine and asparagine oxidations (+15.99 on CKMNPR).
Include deamidation of asparagine and glutamine (NQ-0.98) and pyro-Glu from glutamine (Q-18.01 N-term) as variable modifications.
Enable false discovery rate (FDR) estimation using decoy-fusion algorithm during PEAKS DB search in PEAKS.
